01 · The housing

Clips to the column shroud. Moves with the wheel.

02 · The shift light, assembled

One board instead of a knot of jumper wires.

The carrier replaces a dev board, a CAN breakout, a USB buck module and the harness between them, every joint of which is a thing that vibrates loose in a car. Twelve volts in on a screw terminal; the strip and the bus on two more.

Log it. Read the surface. Flash it.

An Android app that pulls engine telemetry straight from ECU RAM over K-line, fuses it with wideband AFR from the bridge into one time-aligned log, and then writes the calibration changes you decide on back to the EMS2000. Three one-time unlocks on Google Play: the app, the tune options, and the factory software.

Bundled US S, JCW and GP1 images as flash bases. Put a car back to stock, or start a tune from a different factory map.

ECU write needs the App unlock plus either add-on. Flash write needs the facelift silver-cover ECU; logging works on the other boxes. Reads and writes are done key on, engine off, on a battery charger.

Join the tester group $25app unlock $50flash unlock $50factory software Works with a K+DCAN USB cable and USB-C OTG. Works better with the bridge: wideband AFR, CAN channels and the shift light in one log.

In Google Play closed testing, so it does not show up in a Play search. Three steps, all with the Google account on your Android phone:

  1. Join the tester group at groups.google.com/g/r53-logger-testers and tap Join group. It is open, no approval.
  2. Opt in on Play at play.google.com/apps/testing/com.geekopolis.r53logger and tap Become a tester.
  3. Install it from the Play listing. If it says the app is not found, Play is signed in to a different Google account or has not caught up yet; give it a few minutes.

Off-road and competition use. An ECU flash can brick a car; the app backs up the stock BIN first and refuses to write on a shared wire. R53 Coding, the module-coding companion, is a separate app with its own unlock.

05 · Top of the range · K-line + CAN bridge

The shift light grew a second job. Then a third.

One board in the footwell that reads the Siemens EMS2000 over K-line, listens to the CAN bus, and drives the shift light. It plugs into the OBD2 socket and ships raw ECU blocks to your phone over Bluetooth, where the logger does the decoding. It is the best input the logger can have: wideband, CAN channels and the shift light, all in the same time-aligned log.

  • K-line, properly. An ST L9637D transceiver behind a 1 kΩ 1 W pull-up and a 1.5KE27A clamp. DS2 at 9600 baud, 8E1, the ECU's native dialect.
  • CAN, listen-only. RPM, throttle, coolant and road speed off the car's bus, plus AEMnet lambda from a wideband gauge on the same pair. It never ACKs, so it cannot disturb the bus.
  • The shift light, still. Same eight LEDs, straight off CAN RPM. Works with no phone connected and no app running.
  • XIAO ESP32-S3. 8 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM, BLE to the phone.

Fitment

Built on one car. Ours.

2002–06

First-generation MINI Cooper S, chassis R53, the supercharged one. Siemens EMS2000 ECU.

0x316

The CAN id the RPM rides on. The id and the divisor are settings, so a different car is a config change, not a rebuild.

6 of 16

OBD2 pins the bridge uses. CAN is run to pins 6 and 14 so the socket is the single service point.

Does the light work without the phone?

Yes. The strip runs from CAN with no phone and no app. The app only configures and observes. Thresholds saved to the board survive power-off.

Will it upset the car's CAN bus?

No. The node is configured listen-only and never drives a dominant bit, so it cannot acknowledge or disturb the bus. The 120 Ω termination jumper ships open because a vehicle bus is already terminated at both ends.

Why is the iPhone app a web page?

Because Safari has never had Web Bluetooth and every iOS browser has to use Safari's engine. Bluefy bridges it. The web app is the same three screens as Android and is free.

Is the flashing safe?

It is a flash tool for a twenty-year-old ECU, so treat it that way. The app reads and backs up the stock BIN before any write, recomputes the checksum, and refuses to write if anything else is on the K-line. Off-road and competition use only.

Not AWS Route 53?

Not AWS Route 53. R53 is the chassis code.
